text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

-- Parliament on Tuesday passed a law on company bankruptcy in a 60 to 25 vote with 14 abstentions. Critics of the law say the legislation allows state institutions to initiate bankruptcy and call the law "bankruptcy provocation." Supporters of the law say it is an improvement on the old, 1992 legislation.

-- President Algirdas Brazauskas rejected a law on property restitution, passed earlier this month, and sent it back to parliament. It was the sixth law passed by the current parliament that Brazauskas has vetoed.
-- Lithuanian presidential candidate and former deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas leaves for the U.S. to meet American-Lithuanians to gain support for his candidature.
-- In the list of state assets to be privatised in 1997, 835 objects were confirmed but in the first half of the year, only 170 programmes for privatisation were prepared.

-- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG), an applicant for the post of adviser in the Lithuanian Telecom privatisation, will talk to the government about helping to issue government eurbonds in German marks, Piotr Konwicki, a representative of DMG said.
-- Mazheikiu Nafta plans to establish eight to ten U.S.-style container petrol stations in Lithuania and Ukraine, said Leonas Garbenis, deputy economics and finance director of Mazheikiu.
-- The newspaper has been accepted as a member of the European business newspaper federation, which includes the Financial Times, Handelsblatt and Dagens Industri.
-- McDonald's Lithuania, along with similar companies in Latvia and Estonia, will be subordinated to McDonald's Poland.
-- World software giant Microsoft bought two licenses from local firm Fotonija for a Lithuanian language spellcheck.
-- Deputy culture minister Nijole Statkute resigned on Tuesday, the third deputy minister to leave the ministry amid a row with new Culture Minister Saulius Shaltenis.
-- President Brazauskas said Lithuania should wait for Russia to take the first step in recognising Chechnya.
-- Lithuanian scientists dealing with the environment are preparing a book on the consequences of a major accident at the country's Ignalina nuclear power plant.
